=== CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===
- .claude/hooks/pr_merge_status_guard.py:501 | severity=critical | confidence=[5]
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, google_gemini-3_8-flash, minimax_minimax-m3, openai_gpt-6-luna, qwen_qwen3_7-plus, z-ai_glm-5_2]
  PROBLEM: When the remote-config probe exits with a code other than 0 or 1, `_push_targets` treats the positional remote name as a branch refspec instead of requesting confirmation.
  WHY: A probe error can make the guard check the wrong branch and allow a push without evaluating its actual destination; severity was BLOCKER for five reviewers and MAJOR for openai_gpt-6-luna.
- workflow-templates/.claude/hooks/pr_merge_status_guard.py:501 | severity=critical | confidence=[5]
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, google_gemini-3_8-flash, minimax_minimax-m3, openai_gpt-6-luna, qwen_qwen3_7-plus, z-ai_glm-5_2]
  PROBLEM: The template copy has no handling for remote-config probe exit codes other than 0 or 1, so it treats a positional remote name as a branch refspec instead of requesting confirmation.
  WHY: Consumer repos can inherit a guard that checks the wrong branch rather than confirming an unresolved push destination; severity was BLOCKER for five reviewers and MAJOR for openai_gpt-6-luna.
- tests/test_pr_merge_status_guard.py:1015-1028 | severity=high | confidence=[5]
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, qwen_qwen3_7-plus]
  PROBLEM: The regression test for a remote-config probe returning exit 124 and requiring confirmation is absent.
  WHY: Without this test, CI does not cover the probe-error confirmation path, allowing the missing guard to regress undetected.

=== END CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===

=== CONSENSUS TASK GAPS ===
- requirement: If the local remote-config lookup errors rather than reporting no such remote, the guard asks instead of guessing which branch the push targets.
  expected_change_site: `.claude/hooks/pr_merge_status_guard.py:_push_targets` and `workflow-templates/.claude/hooks/pr_merge_status_guard.py:_push_targets`
  confidence=[5]
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, google_gemini-3_8-flash, minimax_minimax-m3, z-ai_glm-5_2]
  EVIDENCE: Lines 495-501 in both guard copies lack the `if code not in (0, 1)` handling; `.claude/hooks/pr_merge_status_guard.py:495-503` and `workflow-templates/.claude/hooks/pr_merge_status_guard.py:495-503` directly execute `refspecs = positionals[1:] if code == 0 else positionals`.
- requirement: A regression test verifies that a remote-config probe error (exit code 124) results in a `permissionDecision: ask` response.
  expected_change_site: `tests/test_pr_merge_status_guard.py`
  confidence=[5]
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, google_gemini-3_8-flash, minimax_minimax-m3, z-ai_glm-5_2]

- requirement: Document in README.md that if the local remote-config lookup errors rather than reporting no such remote, the guard asks instead of guessing which branch the push targets.
  expected_change_site: `README.md`
  confidence=[5]
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, google_gemini-3_8-flash, minimax_minimax-m3, qwen_qwen3_7-plus, z-ai_glm-5_2]

  WHY: If a local branch named `origin` exists and the probe times out, the guard checks branch `origin` instead of requesting confirmation.

  WHY: Consumer repos can check the positional remote name as a branch instead of asking for confirmation.
